sentences.text: Until an editor publishes it, a draft has no page on the public site.
Each save lands on the entry's [holding branch](architecture.md#the-holding-branch), `cairn/<concept>/<id>`, and the public pages are built from the published commit when the site deploys.
A reviewer outside the editor group, such as a board member signing off on a post, therefore has no way to read the draft as the site would show it.
A preview gives that reviewer a private preview link to the draft.
The link opens it as a page of the site at `/preview/<token>`, a route outside the admin, with no sign-in.
The page behind the link reads the draft from its holding branch on every request, and a reviewer who reloads sees the editor's latest save.
It renders the draft through the same composition the public entry pages run, which gives the preview the structure of the page that publishing produces.

The editor's half already ships: every edit screen shows a **Share preview** group in the **Details** slide-over, and [`createCairnAdmin`](../reference/sveltekit.md#createcairnadmin) wires its mint and revoke actions.
Your site adds the two pieces only it can supply.
The first is a `preview_tokens` table in the `AUTH_DB` D1 database, which stores a hash of each link.
The second is a never-prerendered route that renders the draft, mounted inside the same layout group as the entry pages because that group's layouts carry the site's style sheets and chrome.
You apply the preview migration, mount the preview route inside your entry pages' layout group, render the banner, and check that a minted link opens the draft in your site's styles.
A site scaffolded by `create-cairn-site`, the setup command, already carries the migration file, the route, and the banner page.
Its developer applies the migration and goes on to verify, and a hand-built site takes every step.
Because `createCairnAdmin` always wires the group's two actions, the group appears by default.
On a site that has not applied the migration, every mint or revoke from the group answers "The preview_tokens table is missing."
A developer who arrives with that message can finish the setup or hide the group.
[Keep or hide the Share preview group](#keep-or-hide-the-share-preview-group) puts that choice first.

A site that runs a review workflow can mint and revoke links from a custom admin screen on the same table and route, as [Mint and revoke from your admin route](#mint-and-revoke-from-your-admin-route) shows.
The steps assume familiarity with SvelteKit route groups, layouts, and server load functions, with Wrangler's D1 migration commands, and with your site's public entry routes.
No cairn knowledge is assumed beyond your site's admin and its public routes.
The following topics belong to other pages:
Building the public entry route that the preview mirrors belongs to Build the public routes.
How the admin secures its sessions and cookies belongs to [Security model](security-model.md#the-session-cookie).
The admin editor's preview pane, which the adapter's `editor.preview` styles, belongs to [Theme your public site](theme-your-public-site.md#style-the-editor-preview).
**Note:** The link is the credential: anyone who holds it can read the draft without signing in until the link expires, an editor revokes it, or the draft ends.
The preview page reads no cookie and no editor session, so a forwarded link forwards the access with it.
A draft that only signed-in editors may read is not one to share this way.
**Revoke all links** in the **Share preview** group ends every outstanding link for the entry.
The preview needs your site's auth database, its configured origin, and public entry routes built from one config object.
Before you start, confirm that your site has each of the following:
An `AUTH_DB` D1 binding with a `migrations_dir`, where the preview's table goes.
A hand-built site creates it as [Create the auth database](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#create-the-auth-database) shows.
`PUBLIC_ORIGIN` set on the Worker, because every minted link is built from the configured origin and never from the request's host.
[Add the Email Sending binding and name the origin](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#add-the-email-sending-binding-and-name-the-origin) sets it.
Public entry routes built by `createPublicRoutes` from one `PublicRoutesConfig` object.
A scaffolded site keeps that object in `src/chassis/public-routes.ts`.
A hand-built site builds them as Build the public routes describes.
A deployed site, and an editor sign-in that can edit an entry.
The checks in [Verify the preview](#verify-the-preview) use both.
With those in place, the first choice is whether editors see the **Share preview** group during setup.
Every edit screen already shows the **Share preview** group, and until the migration runs, each mint or revoke answers a failure that names the migration.
A site adopting previews keeps the default and goes on to the migration.
To hide the group, follow this step:
If your site is not ready to share previews, in the admin's catch-all page, pass `previewMint={false}` to [`CairnAdmin`](../reference/admin.md#cairnadmin).
A site that renders `EditPage` itself passes the same prop to `EditPage`.
The [`EditPage`](../reference/admin.md#editpage) entry states what hiding the group leaves in place.
The links need a table before anything can mint one.
The `0003_preview.sql` migration adds a `preview_tokens` table to `AUTH_DB` that records each link's hash, its entry, its editor, and its expiry.
The table holds the SHA-256 of each token, never the token itself.
Until the migration runs, the mint and revoke actions answer "The preview_tokens table is missing. Apply migrations/0003_preview.sql to AUTH_DB, then try again."
To apply the migration, follow these steps:
If your site is hand-built, in the project directory, copy `0003_preview.sql` from the package's `migrations/` into your `migrations_dir`:
A scaffolded site's `migrations/` already carries the file.
In the project directory, apply the migrations with `--remote`, and with `--local` for local development:
`<database>` is your D1 database's name.
With the table in place, a minted link still needs a route to open.

Mount [`loadPreview`](../reference/sveltekit.md#loadpreview) at `preview/[token]` inside the same layout group as your entry pages, with `prerender` turned off, so the draft renders in your site's styles.
The style sheets and chrome live on that group's layout chain.
An earlier design rendered previews in a neutral shell and was rejected because drafts rendered unstyled, and a route outside the group reproduces that page.
`loadPreview` and `entryLoad` both run [`composeEntryData`](../reference/delivery.md#composeentrydata), so a preview cannot drift structurally from its public page.
A scaffolded site already keeps its `PublicRoutesConfig` in `src/chassis/public-routes.ts` and already has the route, so its developer can skip these steps.
To mount the route, follow these steps:
If your entry route builds its `PublicRoutesConfig` inline, in a new module, export the object as `publicRoutesConfig`.
If you moved the object, in the entry route, import `publicRoutesConfig` from the new module in place of the inline object.
In the entry pages' group, `src/routes/(site)/` on a scaffolded site, create `preview/[token]/+page.server.ts`.
In that file, export `prerender = false` and a load function that returns `loadPreview(runtime, publicRoutesConfig, event)`.
The scaffold writes the following route file.
The scaffold layers `withReferences` on the result, as its catch-all route does.
A site without that helper returns the result of `loadPreview` directly, as the `loadPreview` entry's example does.
The link is a bearer credential, and a prerendered copy would ship it in a static asset.
The `prerender = false` export rules that out.
If the route is prerendered, `loadPreview` throws a build-time error.
**Warning:** A parent layout's `load` runs for the preview route too, and the data it returns reaches an anonymous link holder.
Keep privileged values out of any layout the preview shares.
In that layout's `load`, branch on `route.id`, or move the pages that need those values into a sibling group.
The preview route never runs a sibling group's layout.
SvelteKit's [Layout data](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/load#Layout-data) documentation describes how layout data reaches a page.
The page now loads the draft, and the banner tells its reader what they are looking at.
In the preview route's `+page.svelte`, [`PreviewBanner`](../reference/public.md#previewbanner) from `@glw907/cairn-cms/public` sits above the article view your entry pages use.
To render the banner, follow this step:
In `preview/[token]/`, create `+page.svelte` that renders `<PreviewBanner preview={data.preview} />` and then your article component.
The scaffold writes the following page.
The scaffold passes `preview` to its `ArticleView`, which then leaves out the canonical link, `og:url`, and the raw-markdown twin link.
The removed `./components` subpath no longer carries `PreviewBanner`.
The banner shows the draft state while the draft exists and an ended state once it is gone.
[Shared link lifecycle](#shared-link-lifecycle) describes both.
A theme whose palette clashes with the banner's defaults can override them.
The banner reads five custom properties, so declaring them on `:root` points it at your tokens without raising specificity.
Their defaults are daisyUI 5 role tokens with no color literal, and on a daisyUI site the banner already follows the theme in every color scheme.
A site without daisyUI points the color properties at its tokens.
Each property sets one part of the banner:
`--cairn-preview-bg` sets the background in both states.
`--cairn-preview-border` sets the border in both states.
`--cairn-preview-fg` sets the text.
`--cairn-preview-link` sets only the ended state's link, since the draft state shows none.
`--cairn-preview-radius` sets the corner radius.
To override the palette, follow this step:
In a style sheet the preview's layout loads, declare the properties on `:root` or on an ancestor of the banner.
Each value stands for a token of your theme.
The `PreviewBanner` entry lists each state's default tokens.
The link's lifetime is the last setting before verification.
A link lasts seven days unless you pass `preview: { ttlMs }` to `createCairnAdmin`, with a value from one minute to thirty days.
To change the lifetime, follow this step:
If seven days does not suit your reviewers, in the module that calls `createCairnAdmin`, add `preview: { ttlMs }` to its config.
On a scaffolded site, that module is `cairn.server.ts` in `src/chassis/`.
`createCairnAdmin` forwards the option unchanged to the content routes.
A site that calls `createContentRoutes` directly passes the same `preview` there.
This `preview` sets only the link's lifetime and is unrelated to the adapter's `editor.preview`, which styles the admin editor's preview pane.
A value outside the range throws an error prefixed `PreviewTokenConfig:` when an editor mints, before any token is generated.
The [`PreviewTokenConfig`](../reference/sveltekit.md#previewtokenconfig) entry records the option.
The whole path, from the edit screen to the rendered page, is now ready to check.
Mint a link for a saved draft, open it with no session, and check that it renders in your site's styles with the preview headers.
To verify the preview on the deployed site, follow these steps:
In the admin, save an edit to an entry, since a mint refuses an entry with no pending draft.
In the editor's **Details** slide-over, in the **Share preview** group, mint a link.
The group shows a link on your configured origin whose path is `/preview/<token>`.
In a private browser window, open the link.
The draft renders in your site's chrome and styles, with the banner above it.
If the page renders unstyled, check the route against [Mount the preview route](#mount-the-preview-route).
In a terminal, print the link's response headers:
Every preview response carries the following headers, refusals included:
`cache-control: private, no-store`
`x-robots-tag: noindex, nofollow`
`referrer-policy: no-referrer`
`x-content-type-options: nosniff`
`x-frame-options: DENY`
In the **Share preview** group, select **Revoke all links**.
In the private window, reload the page.
The page answers 404.
If the link answers an error page at any step, [Diagnose a refused link](#diagnose-a-refused-link) maps the logged reason to a fix.
Once a link is out, the editor's later actions decide what it shows.
A link that stops showing the draft has moved to another state.
It shows the draft while the edit is unpublished, an ended notice once its branch is gone and a live page exists, and a 404 in every other case.
The following cases decide what a link shows:
While the entry's holding branch exists, the link renders the draft.
Publishing the entry, or discarding an edit of an entry that is already live, ends the draft.
The link keeps its row and shows "This preview has ended." with a link to the published page.
The banner never claims the draft went live, because a discarded edit reaches the same state.
Deleting the entry, renaming it, or discarding an entry that was never published clears its links.
A later entry that reuses the id never answers an old link.
Past its lifetime, a link stops resolving.
**Revoke all links** clears every link for the entry at once, and it succeeds even when none is outstanding.
Every case that does not render a page answers the same plain 404, and the visitor never learns which case applied.
Each refused request also writes a log record that names its reason.
Every refused link answers the same 404 except a missing `AUTH_DB` binding, which answers 503.
The reason that the `preview.refused` record carries is therefore the diagnosis.
[Find the records](debug-your-site.md#find-the-records) shows how to find a record by its event name in Workers Logs.
Find the record's reason in the following table.
Reason
What it points at
Fix
`bindings_missing`
The Worker has no `AUTH_DB` binding, and the link answers 503
Bind `AUTH_DB` as [Create the auth database](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#create-the-auth-database) shows
`table_missing`
The `preview_tokens` table does not exist yet
Apply the migration as [Apply the preview migration](#apply-the-preview-migration) shows
`unknown`
No stored link matches, as after a revoke, a delete, a rename, or a never-published discard
Mint a new link
`expired`
The link outlived its lifetime
Mint a new link, or lengthen the lifetime as [Set the link's lifetime](#set-the-links-lifetime) shows
`row_invalid`
The stored concept or id no longer matches the site
Mint a new link from the entry as it stands
`draft_invalid`
The draft on the entry's holding branch fails the concept's validation
In the admin, correct the entry's draft and save it, then reload the link
`branch_gone`
The holding branch is gone and no published file exists
None, since the draft the link shared no longer exists
The `preview.refused` row of [Log events](../reference/log-events.md) lists the fields each reason carries.
A site with a review workflow can mint and revoke links from a custom admin route.
`mintPreview` and `revokePreview` run the built-in actions' checks from a route your site gates, so your workflow can share and take back links.
A site that mounts content routes by hand already gets the built-in `previewMintAction` and `previewRevokeAction` from `createContentRoutes`.
Place and gate the route as [Add a custom admin screen](add-a-custom-admin-screen.md) shows.
Both functions take the editor from the session the admin guard resolves.
The two signatures are `mintPreview(runtime, config, event, { concept, entryId })` and `revokePreview(runtime, event, { concept, entryId })`.
The `config` argument is a `PreviewTokenConfig`, the same `{ ttlMs }` your `createCairnAdmin` call sets.
Both functions check the editor, the concept, the access map, and the id's shape, in that order.
Only then does a mint check for a draft.
A refusal never reveals whether the entry exists.
A session or access-map refusal throws a 403 or a redirect to sign-in.
An unknown concept, a bad id, or, for a mint, a missing draft comes back as an `outcome` value instead.
The [`mintPreview`](../reference/sveltekit.md#mintpreview) and [`revokePreview`](../reference/sveltekit.md#revokepreview) entries list each outcome's fields.
To mint and revoke from your screen, follow these steps:
In your screen's `+page.server.ts`, add an action that calls `mintPreview` with the entry's concept and id.
In that action, when the mint succeeds, build the link from your configured origin, `/preview/`, and the returned token.
In the same file, add an action that calls `revokePreview` with the same concept and id.
The following file shows both actions on a scaffolded site.
The file reads `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` from `cloudflare:workers`.
[Debug your site](debug-your-site.md#eventplatform-is-undefined) explains why the env comes from there.
Both functions log the same mint and revoke records the built-in actions log.
The `sharePreview` action returns a link that opens the draft, the same result [Verify the preview](#verify-the-preview) checks.
The following pages cover the functions, the component, and the records this page uses:
[Public preview](../reference/sveltekit.md#public-preview): the `loadPreview`, `mintPreview`, and `revokePreview` entries.
[`PreviewBanner`](../reference/public.md#previewbanner): the banner's props and default tokens.
[Log events](../reference/log-events.md): the `preview.refused` row and the token mint and revoke rows.
[Add a custom admin screen](add-a-custom-admin-screen.md): the screen a custom mint lives on.
[Security model](security-model.md): how the admin's sessions are secured.

cuts.reason: This is a writing constraint, not a page claim. The preview steps touch the runtime and publicRoutesConfig, never the adapter file. If the drafter names the adapter, it must say which site it means.
